Round 376 is stopped and waiting for two rulings from B. The sketch is applied and every check I ran passed, but I have not marked the round complete.

**Stop 1: TC10 is too close to its time limit.** This test is in `transport-centre-ui.test.tsx`, a file this round did not change, and it uses vitest's default 5 s limit.
- In the 140-file run it took 3.09 s, which is 62 % of the limit.
- At gate 375 it took 2.10 s (42 %). Lesson L11 says the higher time decides, so it is over the 50 % line.
- Run on its own it takes about 1.46 s, against 1.32 s on a copy of the previous published code. So this round adds about 10 %, and most of the 3.09 s comes from the load of the full run.

**Stop 2: the code-reviewer raised a Medium about the test file B's sketch changed.** The new render-count test never makes two edits in a row with the same Undo label. So nothing proves that Undo, Redo, Split and Delete keep the same function identity across edits. If they did not, the Edit group (the Undo/Redo/Split/Delete buttons) would re-render on every edit. The worst case is a slower Studio, not wrong behaviour. The test files must stay identical to B's sketch, so I did not add the test the reviewer proposed; B decides whether it is needed.

The reviewer's second Medium is that the focus hand-off expires after one frame, which only works if those actions update the screen immediately when clicked. Nothing on that path defers the update today. I wrote this assumption into the implementation doc; the code is unchanged.

**Done:**
- **Sketch:** its checksum matched B's, it applied cleanly, and all six files match B's hashes. I made no other edits to them, and no protected file was touched.
- **Checks:**
  - `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` passed. Lint shows 205 warnings across the repo, none in the changed files.
  - Biome on the six files reports no problems.
  - All 140 covering files pass: 2,200 tests.
- **New doc** `docs/implementation/2026/quarter-IV/243-perf-transport-leaves.md`:
  - Line 4 is exactly the required status line, and the headings follow the template.
  - The mutant list names the tests that actually failed in B's mutant logs, not the ones the task table predicted.
- **Review:**
  - The code-reviewer found nothing Critical or High; its Low findings are listed for B.
  - I changed the doc after the review, so it got a second review, which found no errors.
  - The reviewer's architecture note goes to B: there are now three `use*Actions` hooks in StudioWorkspace. The reviewer says keep them for now and handle it under ARCH-CHECKPOINT-PERF11C-LEAF-PLUMBING.

I did not run the full suite, `npm run verify`, the build, perf, the mutants or any browser checks; those belong to C and the gate. The report is `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-376.md`, with the exact next checks for C. Logs are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-376/`.
